clue.text: He gives the orders for heavy artillery fire

definitions.meaning: an important person in charge, a bigwig
read literally, a large cannon round

explanation.surface: A commander directs his gunners to open up with the heavy guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a powerful boss, and literally a large projectile from a big gun.

clue.text: They prohibit signs of protest

definitions.meaning: people who ban things
placards carried at a demonstration

explanation.surface: Placards being outlawed at a demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as people who ban, and also the placards held up on marches.

clue.text: Reveal intention to let the other fellow win

definitions.meaning: to let slip a secret plan

definitions.text: to let the other fellow win
definitions.meaning: literally, to concede a match to an opponent

explanation.surface: Showing your hand by allowing the rival to triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for betraying a secret plan, and read literally, throwing a match.

clue.text: A woman's love makes him man of the hour

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Being loved by a woman makes a man the centre of attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated person admired for a great deed.

clue.text: Crack-down on credit leads to rebuke

indicators.note: in a down clue on places one piece below, so after, the other

parts.note: tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick
a crackdown switches something off

explanation.surface: A clampdown on lending leads to a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: Buying 'on tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to scold or reprimand.

clue.text: Undergarment for Lady Diana

definitions.meaning: a short close-fitting vest or bodice worn under clothes
Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A piece of lingerie destined for the royal bride.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Diana Spencer married Prince Charles in 1981, around when this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: A spencer is a woollen under-vest, and it was the maiden surname of the late Princess of Wales.

clue.text: Porter takes in work, despite order to continue striking

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, like stout
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A railway porter takes on work in defiance of a call to stay on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' suggests a station worker, but it is the beer. 'despite order' adds that strikers stay out after being told to return.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain away from work on strike.

clue.text: Like to write in Early English for relaxation

indicators.note: the second piece is written inside the first

parts.note: as means like

explanation.surface: A suggestion to compose in Middle Ages English to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease means rest or freedom from effort.

clue.text: Drinks beer after time the result of business failure?

indicators.note: after puts the drinks pieces behind the time piece

parts.note: closing time, when the pub shuts
downs means drinks, swallows
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A drinker downs beer after hours, which is what bankrupts the business.
explanation.definitionFit: A clearance sale held when a shop shuts for good.

clue.text: Shot through when Lorna's Jan took command

parts.note: John (Jan) Ridd is the hero who loves Lorna in R.D. Blackmore's novel Lorna Doone
led means took command

explanation.surface: Someone was shot when Jan took charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorna Doone is a Victorian novel set on Exmoor; its narrator John Ridd is called Jan in dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierced with many holes, as by bullets.

clue.text: Total unanimity, but that's no puzzle at all

definitions.meaning: the phrase describes people who have never once quarrelled
read literally, something that is not ever a grid of clues

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees completely, so there is nothing to puzzle over.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means perfect harmony without any argument; split differently it denies being a puzzle.

clue.text: They may include some meat sandwiches

definitions.text: They may include some meat sandwiches

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that a selection of food may feature meat sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'They may include' cannot stand for food on its own; the whole clue defines the answer while 'some' picks out the run inside 'meat sandwiches'.
explanation.definitionFit: Snacks or food in general, which could well feature a few meat sandwiches.

clue.text: Quite unacceptable, whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: the letters give the same phrase whether read forwards or backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something is simply not acceptable from any angle.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something that is not permissible or not done.

clue.text: Tyndale's Testament

definitions.meaning: William Tyndale, the Bible translator, whose first name shortens to this
a document disposing of a person's property after death

explanation.surface: A reference to the New Testament translated by William Tyndale.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyndale's English Testament makes the solver think of scripture, but Testament here is a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: The familiar short form of William, Tyndale's first name, and the legal document sometimes called a last testament.

clue.text: Rash complaint from honey producers

definitions.meaning: an itchy skin eruption, urticaria
beehives produce honey

explanation.surface: An ill-considered grievance from beekeepers.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term for nettle rash, and the plural of bee boxes.

clue.text: Steal, but only very little

definitions.meaning: to nick or steal
a tiny amount, as of salt

explanation.surface: Thieving, but just a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for stealing, and a tiny quantity held between finger and thumb.

clue.text: He can enforce the law if fresh changes are made

indicators.note: the letters of the words before are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A lawman is able to keep order provided new reforms happen.
explanation.definitionFit: A county or town officer responsible for keeping the peace.

clue.text: Thickhead got severely reprimanded but understood why

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of the word thick
wigged is old slang for scolded, from a wigging

explanation.surface: A dimwit was given a dressing-down but at least grasped the reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thickhead' looks like an insult but gives only its head letter. A wigging is British slang for a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for realised or caught on to the reason.

clue.text: Strike a bargain to hand players their cards

definitions.meaning: to agree terms in a business arrangement
to distribute the cards at the start of a game

explanation.surface: Reaching an agreement and then dealing out a hand of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for agreeing terms, and literally performing one dealing round in a card game.

clue.text: Prophet of more godly disposition

definitions.meaning: a seer who foretells the future
comparative of divine, more godly

explanation.surface: A seer with a holier temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothsayer, and the comparative form of divine meaning holier.

clue.text: How to touch on a sore point frivolously

definitions.text: How to touch on a sore point
definitions.meaning: gently, without pressing
without seriousness

explanation.surface: Advice on raising a delicate subject in a light-hearted way.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning gently, and also flippantly or without gravity.

clue.text: Fine performers' agents

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
actors are stage performers

explanation.surface: Admirable representatives looking after actors.
explanation.walkthrough: Factors are agents, chiefly estate managers in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Factors are people who act for others in business, synonyms of representatives.

clue.text: Forge ten fair paintings

indicators.note: to forge is to shape anew, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Counterfeiting ten good pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings are works of the visual arts, the high-art category.

clue.text: Second victory by fellow in Wiltshire

parts.note: a win is a victory
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: Another triumph by a man in a West Country county.
explanation.walkthrough: SWINDON is a large town in Wiltshire, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway town in that English county.

clue.text: We return after six to watch TV

indicators.note: after places the turned word behind the numeral

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: return asks for the word we to be turned round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: We come home after six o'clock to sit in front of the television.
explanation.definitionFit: To view is to look at a programme, as viewers do.

clue.text: One empowered to get old biblical books

parts.note: to age is to grow old
NT is the New Testament, a group of biblical books

explanation.surface: Someone given authority to fetch ancient scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: A person authorised to act on behalf of another, as a representative.

clue.text: In the meantime he's joined the Opposition

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Meanwhile a politician has crossed over to the other side of the House.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is against a cause, an opponent.

clue.text: Bridge bidding convention resulting in a pass

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A bidding system at the card table leads to a pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' suggests a bridge call; here it is a gap between peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A widely used system of bidding in contract bridge, named after a London club.

clue.text: A paper boss with one recurrent thought

indicators.note: recurrent means running back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor and a single nagging notion that keeps returning.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion or concept in the mind.

clue.text: Met, office put fresh tax on ground storage area

parts.note: new means fresh
scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free
land is ground
a yard is an enclosed area for storing materials

explanation.surface: A forecasting office levies fresh taxes on land used for storage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met office' suggests the British weather service, but the Met is London's Metropolitan Police, headquartered at this building.
explanation.definitionFit: The headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police force.

clue.text: Crown commission?

definitions.meaning: the monarchy, the sovereign and family
a payment made to an author or inventor on each sale

explanation.surface: Is the monarchy taking a cut?
explanation.definitionFit: The royal family as an institution, and a fee paid per copy sold to a writer.

clue.text: I daren't exchange one car for another

indicators.note: exchange asks for the letters of the words before to swap places

explanation.surface: A nervous motorist dare not swap an old vehicle for a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange' looks like part of the definition but is the anagram signal; what remains describes the deal of offering an old car against a new one.
explanation.definitionFit: An old vehicle handed over in part-payment for a new one.
